html:
The Way of the Celestial Masters is the oldest organised school of Daoist religion. It was founded in 142 CE in Sichuan by Zhang Daoling, who said the deified Laozi had appeared to him and named him the first Celestial Master.

His followers paid a fee of five pecks of rice to join, which gave the movement its early nickname. They confessed their sins to be healed, and were organised into parishes under priests called libationers, with charity inns for travellers.

Near the end of the Han dynasty, Zhang Daoling's grandson Zhang Lu ruled a small religious state in the Hanzhong area for over twenty years, at the same time as the Yellow Turban Rebellion shook the east. In 215 he surrendered to the warlord Cao Cao, who moved many followers north, spreading the faith across China.

The line of Celestial Masters continued for centuries, later based at Mount Longhu in Jiangxi. After 1949 the line moved to Taiwan. Many of the rituals of Daoism today go back to this movement.
